Definition: to howl (with a wailing tone) or yell (with a boisterous one)
BiblicalUsage: Yâlal is the howl of grief, the wailing that breaks out when judgment falls. Amos hears the songs of the temple turned to howlings, and Ezekiel is told to cry and howl because the sword is coming upon the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe grief has a sound in Scripture, and God does not ask His people to suffer in silence.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
